eyebrow: Rendez-vous — one room, one agent, one artifact, many members
title: Work is multiplayer. Agents are single-player.
bullets: Every agent you use today lives in exactly one person's window.
So the human becomes the integration layer: copy-paste between two chat windows.
A screenshot forwarded to the other side. “Let me ask the AI and get back to you.”
The second person never sees the context.
The deliverable dies inside one private thread.

title: Four members. Four surfaces. One session.

ladderRows.sends: the commit log, the files, what the laptop knows
ladderRows.receives: the same transcript as the humans
the PDF, once a member confirms

caption: Julie and Tom are organising the company offsite. Neither installed anything, neither shares a login, and Atlas — an agent on the company Mac — opens the room because it noticed the deadline. The room models members, not humans, which is why a machine joins the way a person does.

eyebrow: It works — live, on real surfaces
title: Not a mock. A real phone, a real thread, a real artifact.

timelineItems.label: A real phone types “new” on Telegram — the room exists
Cold boot: agent session and shared artifact both ready
A laptop joins; one agent reply reaches both surfaces, each message tagged with who sent it and from where
The agent edits the shared artifact on request — confirmed on the URL while the phone thread continues
A PDF previewed, confirmed with a token, rendered — and byte-matched in the inbox
The sandbox deleted out from under the room; the sweep caught it and the next message revived it
voice in · photo in · a private “@me” answer · a voice reply · real files attached · a desktop agent joining as a member · resume replaying the prior transcript

caption: The rows above the line are in the rehearsal log with timestamps. The row below it is built and tested, and you watch it happen — real screens, one take. We keep the two apart on purpose.

eyebrow: The stack, and what it cost to trust it
title: Eight silent failures. Seven pull requests upstream.
bullets: A killed session still answers 200 — resume reported success in 0.7s having resumed nothing.
Omit one flag and a message arriving mid-turn is lost; the sender sees it sent.
A paused sandbox expires and the room keeps handing people its dead link.
None crash. Four lost data quietly. All look like working code or correct config.
code:
Telegram · Email · Web · a desktop agent
        ↓
  [ agentpush ]     every channel behind one API, in and out
        ↓
 [ RENDEZ-VOUS ]    members · attribution · fan-out · authority
        ↓
  [ agentproto ]    our runtime — unmodified, from npm
        ↓
     [ e2b ]        one sandbox, one artifact URL
highlight: Day-one rule: never fork, never vendor, never patch the runtime. Eight findings later it held — every fix went upstream with a test that reproduces the failure first.

eyebrow: Work leaves the room — on purpose
title: A room with a notion of authority, not a relay.

findingsItems.label: A member asks the room for the deliverable — a PDF of what everyone just built
the room previews it first: recipient, channel, subject, the rendered document — and sends nothing until a member explicitly confirms
it lands on a phone as a real PDF and in an inbox — recipient, subject and contents exactly as previewed
the send is written into the shared transcript: who asked, who confirmed, what, to whom

highlight: Every other capability keeps work inside the room. This one lets it leave — under the members' control, on the record.

title: Eight findings, and where each fix landed.

findingsItems.label: a mid-turn prompt is lost without queue: true, and a killed session still answers 200 so resume reports success doing nothing
sandbox liveness unreported; orphaned boxes never reaped; a failed reconnect leaves the box running and billing
app serve ignores the declared UI path; a mutating proxy route had no auth gate
the fan-out cursor froze on resume, the artifact link outlived its box, and a recap fix shipped dead on arrival — each now has a regression test
an account-pinned inbound route never fires; the agent proposes rebuilding a capability the workspace already brokered

highlight: The recap fix is the one worth telling: its first version never ran, hid behind a reply that looked exactly like success, and 443 passing tests never caught it. A local harness did.
caption: This is why the room records who asked, who confirmed, and what was sent. Where failure is silent, the transcript is the only thing checkable afterwards.

title: What we have not proven.
bullets: Paused sandboxes expire in 20–60 minutes. One did, live, mid-rehearsal — the room advertised a dead link until we made box liveness its own fact.
WhatsApp is not provisioned: no number, no key. The room is channel-agnostic by construction, so it is a config change, not code.
We share an existing workspace's Telegram routing; a catch-all route there could fire alongside ours.
Swapping the runtime for Codex failed at the auth gate, not the swap — a fresh box has no login. The credential model is the real work.
